abstract: Linear B-cell epitopes are antigenic regions recognised by antibodies that play crucial roles in vaccine development, antibody production, and other therapeutic applications.Their prediction can support peptide-based vaccine candidate screening and diagnostic assay development, but the experimental data required for model development may be distributed across institutions that cannot freely pool their records. We present FedEpitope, a federated framework that adapts the ESM-2 protein language model for peptide-level linear B-cell epitope prediction using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), keeping client-partitioned data local and restricting the communicated trainable model state to approximately 1.11 MB. Simulated benchmarks of FedAvg and FedProx algorithms, evaluated using homology-aware data splits of five biologically heterogeneous, organism-partitioned clients, achieve promising global test performance without centralising training data, with FedAvg outperforming all single-client models in mean AP, F1, and MCC. Additional experiments characterise post-federation personalisation, record-level differential privacy, sensitivity to controlled client heterogeneity, LoRA rank, and generalisation to the independent BCPreds and NetBCE benchmarks, demonstrating the feasibility of parameter-efficient federated protein language model adaptation for data-localised B-cell epitope prediction and the associated trade-offs among predictive performance, personalisation, privacy, communication efficiency, and distribution shift.
